```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

# Plan:
# Create the bundles
# Limit the bundles to ones we can afford (exactly afford or underspend?)
# Examine which bundle design methodologies we can accommodate
# See which bundle designs are most efficient
# Determine how many qs must be asked to reach desired statistical power

```

```{r Create the Bundles}
# Load the library for efficient DCE bundle design
library(cbcTools)
library(ggplot2)

# Initalize the features and levels into "profiles" AKA bundles.
# In the experiment participants will choose between two bundles and a default.

# Generate the bundles with cbc_profiles
totalprofiles <- cbc_profiles(
  participants  = c("p0", "p150", "p300"),
  community     = c("c0", "c815", "c3578"),
  policy        = c("pnoresults0", "preport0", "p3500"),
  compensation  = c("comp0", "comp600", "comp1200"),
  research      = c("r0", "r700", "r1400", "r2100", "r2800", "r3500", "r4200", "r4900")
)
```
# Features Need Descriptive Names

```{r Estimate Cost And Drop Expensive Bundles}
library(dplyr)
# Set the budget value
budget = 5000

# Initialize a column which sums the cost each feature level per profile
totalprofiles$costsum <- 0

# For each feature, increment the total cost by how much that bundle cost 
# by each feature.
totalprofiles <- totalprofiles %>%
  mutate(costsum = costsum + case_when(
    participants == "p0" ~ 0,
    participants == "p150" ~ 150,
    participants == "p300" ~ 300
  ))

totalprofiles <- totalprofiles %>%
  mutate(costsum = costsum + case_when(
    community == "c0" ~ 0,
    community == "c815" ~ 815,
    community == "c3578" ~ 3578
  ))

totalprofiles <- totalprofiles %>%
  mutate(costsum = costsum + case_when(
    policy == "pnoresults0" ~ 0, 
    policy == "preport0" ~ 0,
    policy == "p3500" ~ 3500
  ))

totalprofiles <- totalprofiles %>%
  mutate(costsum = costsum + case_when(
    compensation == "comp0" ~ 0,
    compensation == "comp600" ~ 600,
    compensation == "comp1200" ~ 1200
  ))

#Use the profile cost up to this point to initialize a set of profiles that will
#set whatever funding is leftover as the amount spent on research. See next code
#chunk for handling continuous research funding
initialstrictbudgetprofiles <- totalprofiles %>% select(-research)

#Finish up with the discrete research costs
totalprofiles <- totalprofiles %>%
  mutate(costsum = costsum + case_when(
    research == "r0" ~ 0,
    research == "r700" ~ 700,
    research == "r1400" ~ 1400,
    research == "r2100" ~ 2100,
    research == "r2800" ~ 2800,
    research == "r3500" ~ 3500,
    research == "r4200" ~ 4200,
    research == "r4900" ~ 4900
  ))

# Subset only the profiles are within the budget
affordableprofiles <- subset(totalprofiles, costsum <= budget)


# Drop the costsum column now that we've excluded the overly expensive options.
# profilestoprocess will be put through the next cbcTools functions
profilestoprocess <- affordableprofiles %>% select(-costsum)
```

```{r Strict Budget Alternative}
# The strictbudgetprofiles dataset does not yet include the cost of additional funding. 
# Filter out bundles that are alredy too expensive, and set the research column
# Equal to the remainder, such that the total cost sums to the budget

# Initialize the research feature
initialstrictbudgetprofiles$research <- NA

# Subset strictbudgetprofiles to only allow for budgets that don't already exceed
# The budget set out before research costs are considered
strictbudgetprofiles <- unique(subset(initialstrictbudgetprofiles, costsum <= budget))

# Now these profiles/bundles are all affordable, calculate leftover funds for research
# These values will be zero or positive since we have already filtered 
# overly expensive designs
strictbudgetprofiles$research <- budget - strictbudgetprofiles$costsum

# Prep profiles for design function by removing costsum column.
# Note that the costsum column would equal the budget if we had incremeneted with
# the cost of research after we calculated it, but this step is unnecessary in 
# our case since we already know we can afford the bundles. They equal the budget
strictbudgetprofiles <- strictbudgetprofiles %>% select(-costsum)

#If strict budgeting is desired, uncomment the following line
# profilestoprocess <- strictbudgetprofiles

```

```{r Generate bundle designs}
# Generate survey designs from the profilestoprocess

# This will generate bundle designs from whatever profile set provided. 
# Ensure that profilestoprocess is the name of the desired profile set
# before proceeding.

# Set the number of respondents and questions per respondent
numparticipants = 400
numqs = 20

# Set the number of alternatives equal to two for binary choice
numalts = 2

# Set to TRUE if a "no choice" option is permitted
inclnochoice = TRUE

# Denote features with a column vector
features <- c("participants", "community", "policy", "research", "compensation")
best_fit_full <- 1000
best_se_yet <- 1000
best_fit_rand <- 1000
best_fit_dopt <- 1000
i = 1

# Generate a full factorial design
for (i in 1:20) {
fullfac_design <- cbc_design(
profiles = profilestoprocess,
n_resp = numparticipants, # Number of respondents
n_alts = numalts, # Number of alternatives per question
n_q = i, # Number of questions per respondent
#no_choice = inclnochoice, # Whether a "no choice" option is permitted
method = 'full' #Full-factorial design
)

# Obtain power for each design by simulating choices
fullfac_data <- cbc_choices(
  design = fullfac_design,
  obsID = "obsID"
)

power_fullfac <- 
  cbc_power(
    data = fullfac_data,
    pars = features, #Set parameters to the features
    outcome = "choice",
    obsID = "obsID",
    nbreaks = 50,
    n_q = i,
    n_cores = 1
  )

average_se_given_i_full_fac = sum(power_fullfac$se)/nrow(power_fullfac)

cat("The average SE for ", i, "questions per participant is ", average_se_given_i_full_fac)
if(average_se_given_i_full_fac < best_se_yet) {best_fit_full = i}
i <- i + 1
}



# Generate a random design
best_se_yet <- 1000
for (i in 1:20) {
  
  random_design <- cbc_design(
  profiles = profilestoprocess,
  n_resp = numparticipants, # Number of respondents
  n_alts = numalts, # Number of alternatives per question
  n_q = i, # Number of questions per respondent
  #no_choice = inclnochoice, # Whether a "no choice" option is permitted
  method = 'random' #random selection design
  )

random_data <- cbc_choices(
  design = random_design,
  obsID = "obsID"
)

power_random <- random_design |>
  cbc_choices(obsID = "obsID") |>
  cbc_power(
    pars = features, #Set parameters to the features
    outcome = "choice",
    obsID = "obsID",
    nbreaks = 50,
    n_q = i,
    n_cores = 1
  )

average_se_given_i_rand = sum(power_random$se)/nrow(power_random)

cat("With ", i, "questions per participant:")
print(power_random)

i <- i + 1
}

best_se_yet <- 1000

dopt_design <- cbc_design(
  profiles = profilestoprocess,
  n_resp = 400, # Number of respondents
  n_alts = numalts, # Number of alternatives per question
  n_q = 10, # Number of questions per respondent
  n_blocks = 8,
  #no_choice = inclnochoice, # Whether a "no choice" option is permitted
  method = 'dopt' #random selection design
)

dopt_design_long <- dopt_design %>%
  # Pivot the specified columns to a long format
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("participants") | starts_with("community") | 
           starts_with("policy") | starts_with("compensation") | 
           starts_with("research"),
    names_to = "category",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  # Extract the main category and numeric part
  mutate(
    main_category = str_extract(category, "^[^_]+"),   # Extract text before the first underscore
    value = ifelse(value == 1, str_extract(category, "[^_]+$"), NA)  # Keep value only if present
  ) %>%
  # Filter out NA values
  filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
  # Pivot wider to have one column per main category
  select(-category) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = main_category,
    values_from = value
  )

dopt_data <- cbc_choices(
  design = dopt_design,
  obsID = "obsID"
)

power_dopt <- dopt_design |>
  cbc_choices(obsID = "obsID") |>
  cbc_power(
    pars = features, #Set parameters to the features
    outcome = "choice",
    obsID = "obsID",
    nbreaks = 50,
    n_q = 10,
    n_cores = 1
  )

average_se_given_i_dopt = sum(power_dopt$se)/nrow(power_dopt)

cat("The average SE for ", i, "questions per participant is ", average_se_given_i_dopt)
if(average_se_given_i_dopt < best_se_yet) {best_fit_dopt = i}
i <- i + 1


plot_compare_power(power_fullfac, power_random, power_dopt)

```
